“Her story is the story of Indian textiles..”
Weaving a legacy by Radhika Singh

Suraiya Hasan Bose wasn’t just a revivalist, she was a force who breathed life back into India’s textile heritage. From reimagining handlooms in Andhra Pradesh to becoming a key Fabindia supplier, her legacy is woven into the very fabric of our journey.

Her deep connection with the land and its crafts is truly inspirational. “She knew every leaf on that land and would have been aware of the loss of even one flower if someone had plucked it.” That same care and attention translated into how she reimagined weaving, reconstructing fabrics, adjusting thread counts, and helping redefine the handloom landscape in Andhra Pradesh.

She was a force to be reckoned with and celebrated across the globe.

We are deeply saddened by the passing of Andrew Kassoy, co-founder of B Lab and the visionary behind the B Corp movement.
His unwavering belief that business can be a force for good, serving people and the planet, has reshaped the way many of us think about leadership and impact.

We have been fortunate to be associated with the B Corp movement for nearly a decade. In 2015, Organic India USA proudly became a Certified B Corporation and has continued to be among the top-rated B Corps globally. More recently, one of our associate company, Rangsutra Crafts, also achieved B Corp Certification becoming one of the few B Corps in India.

Being part of this powerful global community, built on the foundation of nurturing people, planet, and purpose, has been a privilege and a source of continuous inspiration. It is a movement that reflects Andrew’s visionary leadership and commitment to creating systems that serve the greater good.

Andrew’s legacy will continue to inspire purpose-driven work around the world. We are honored to carry his vision forward through our work, and we believe his impact will echo through the generations to come.

Our heartfelt condolences go out to his family, colleagues, and everyone whose lives he touched.

On his 100th birthday, we celebrate the inspiring life and enduring vision of Shri L.C. Jain. A towering figure whose principles were forged in the Gandhian movement, Mr. Jain dedicated his early life to compassionate service, playing a vital role in the resettlement of refugees during Partition.

He was also a true champion of the artisan community, developing and nurturing India’s incredible handloom and handicraft sector. As the young leader of the Handicrafts and Handlooms Exports Corporation (HHEC) and the Central Cottage Industries Corporation, he helped put India’s crafts on the global map.

The connection between Shri L.C. Jain and Fabindia is personal and profound. Our founder, Mr. John Bissell, found a guide and friend in Mr. Jain while working at HHEC. He did more than introduce John to the vast and varied crafts of India; he became a treasured mentor whose wisdom shaped the very foundation of Fabindia’s Mission. It was also at the HHEC office that Mr. Bissell met his future wife and partner, Mrs. Bim Bissell.

We are deeply grateful for the inspired path Mr. Jain paved. His legacy of integrity, service, and commitment to India’s weavers and artisans continues to inspire every thread we weave and every pattern we print today.

Once again, it’s our privilege to celebrate the 100th Birth Anniversary of a true icon.

This World Environment Day, Fabindia is joining hands with the United Nations Environment Programme for a healthier future by embracing conscious, community-driven choices.

At Fabindia, sustainability isn’t a trend — it’s our tradition.
• 95–100% of our raw materials are of natural origin
• 67% of our products are made using hand-based processes
• By using 20,00,000 wooden hangers, we’ve prevented 100 metric tonnes of plastic waste
• We support over 55,000 rural artisans, creating slow, meaningful fashion that respects both people and planet

We’re committed to:
• Minimizing plastic across our supply chain
• Using biodegradable, reusable, or recycled packaging
• Offering natural, sustainable alternatives for your wardrobe, home, and personal care
• Supporting India’s craft communities — the original custodians of sustainable living
Because if we keep going the way we are, our oceans will carry more packaging than marine life.
It’s time to protect what inspires us — nature.

We extend our heartiest congratulations to Ms. Poonam Muttreja on being appointed as the Chairperson of Dastkar.

She takes the baton from Ms. Laila Tyabji, Padma Shri awardee, Indian social worker, designer, writer, and co-founder of Dastkar, who has spent over four decades championing the hands that create. Both their journeys with Dastkar reflect a deep-rooted commitment to India’s craft communities.

As one of Dastkar’s founding members in 1981, Ms Muttreja has worked extensively across institution-building, philanthropy, innovation, teaching, mentoring, and the scaling of evidence-based programmes. She has also co-founded and led several influential organisations, including the Ashoka Foundation and the Society for Rural, Urban and Tribal Initiative (SRUTI).

As the Executive Director of the Population Foundation of India (PFI), a leading organisation advancing gender-sensitive policies and programmes, she continues to promote the health and well-being of India’s population, particularly women and young people.

At Fabindia, we celebrate her lifelong commitment to community building and social impact. Together, we continue to dream of an India where every artisan is celebrated, and every handmade tradition finds its rightful place in the sun.

At just 12, Pandi Ram Mandavi began learning the secrets of tribal woodcraft from his father and grandfather in Narayanpur, Bastar. What began as a child’s initiation into tradition soon became a lifelong devotion to craft and culture.

Today at 68, honored with the Padma Shri and affectionately known as the “Shilp Guru”, he stands as the torchbearer of Gond Muria artistry. From reviving Bastar’s wooden sculptures and embossed paintings to keeping alive the soulful Sulur flute, Mandavi has carved a language that speaks beyond borders.

“All credit goes to my father,” he shares, carrying forward a legacy that has outlived struggle, insurgency, and time itself.

From Narayanpur to Naples, his creations have travelled across continents, finding space in museum halls, luxury hotels, and cultural showcases. He didn’t speak the same language as his audiences, yet his art needed no translation.

By training more than 1,000 artisans, he has ensured that Bastar’s voice will never fade but will echo through every generation.

Often called “soft gold,” cashmere is the ultimate expression of weightless warmth, harvested from the delicate undercoat of goats that roam the frost-shattered peaks of Central Asia.

This noble fibre takes its very name from the Kashmir region, the historic heart of the trade where centuries-old artisanal mastery first transformed raw fleece into the world’s most coveted textiles.

Its legendary status is owed to a fibre so incredibly fine it that it can be threaded through a ring, smoothly and it also creates a thermal embrace up to eight times warmer than wool, yet feels as ethereal as a second skin.

To wear it is to experience a heritage of absolute refinement—a rare, tactile indulgence that remains the gold standard of quiet, conscious luxury.

Fabindia takes great care to wrap and pack your cashmere shawls and stoles with love and care.

A Celebration of Chanderi & Fabindia

What started as a journey over 2 decades ago has reached a platform that celebrates the 4 pillars of Chanderi’s continued growth - Weavers, Administration, Banking & Finance and the Markets.

It was a privilege for Fabindia to be a key part of the ‘Chanderi Eco Retreat and Fest’, that commenced on November 28th and beautifully commemorated the rich craft and cultural heritage of Chanderi. The event also served as a celebration of the town’s famed weaves, set against the backdrop of its magnificent historical landmarks like the colossal Kati Ghati rock-cut gateway, the regal Kila Kothi and its numerous ancient Mahals.

The full day of celebrations honouring Chanderi’s unique heritage began with a heartfelt exchange: Mr. Bissell had an elaborate discussion with the master weavers associated with Fabindia, where they reminisced about the collaboration and shared ideas to put Chanderi on the global map.

Following this artisan meet, the official event commenced with an Inaugural Address by the Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav via a video message. The Union Minister of Communication and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia, graced the occasion as the Chief Guest and was joined on the dais by Mr. Bissell.

The formal session was followed by a crucial round table discussion with key stakeholders.

The night concluded with the grand finale of the day: a spectacular fashion show titled, “Threads of Time: The Chanderi Saga,” dedicated to Chanderi’s traditional weaving and its unique heritage. It was made more magical with Live Sufi Music that matched the vibrance of the garments. 

Fabindia had the honor of opening the show and presenting a specially curated collection inspired by the exquisite textures, motifs, and weaving traditions of Chanderi expressed across Indian, Fusion and Western Wear.
